[[No overall control]]{{efn|Labour minority.}} | after_election = | after_party = }} The '''2026 Rushmoor Borough Council election''' took place on '''7 May 2026''' to elect councillors to [[Rushmoor Borough Council]] in [[Hampshire]], England. The election was held on the same day as other [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|local elections across England]].{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Rushmoor elections and voting |url=https://www.rushmoor.gov.uk/your-council/elections-and-voting/voting/ |access-date=29 January 2026 |work=Rushmoor Borough Council |date=29 January 2026}} Rushmoor Borough Council is elected by thirds. One councillor in each of the borough’s 13 wards will be elected, with councillors serving four-year terms. The seats contested at this election were last contested in 2022. == Summary == ===Background=== In the previous 2024 election, the Labour Party gained control of the council for the first time, winning a majority of seats from the Conservative Party.{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Labour gain first win in rushmoor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cv27184xxp3o |access-date=29 January 2026 |work=BBC |date=3 May 2024}} During the 2024–2026 council term, several councillors changed their party affiliation. Some Labour councillors resigned from the party in 2025, citing differences over local priorities and governance, forming the Rushmoor Independent Group. This led to the council falling into no overall control, with the Labour group holding power as a minority administration.{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title=Labour loses council control after resignations |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c2enem0dm4jo|access-date=29 January 2026 |work=BBC |date=2 September 2025}} ===Election result=== {{Election summary partial council net
